title: How to pay contractors in Colombia from a US company (2026)
summary: Pay contractors in Colombia from the US: W-8BEN, no 1099, DIAN and RUT invoicing, IVA on exports, misclassification rules and payout options compared.
body_markdown:
*Updated October 2026*


**The short answer:** a US company can pay a contractor in Colombia directly in US dollars. Collect a Form W-8BEN, skip the 1099, sign a services agreement that reflects real independence, and let the contractor invoice you under their DIAN registration (RUT). Pick a payment rail that shows the full FX cost before you send.


Colombia has become one of the default places US startups go when they need senior talent in their own time zone. The paperwork is lighter than most founders expect, but it sits on two sides of the border at once: what the IRS expects from you, and what Colombia's tax authority, DIAN, expects from the person you pay. Get both right and paying a developer in Medellín feels like paying a vendor in Miami. If you are still choosing between contractors and employees, start with our[Colombia hiring and payroll guide](https://www.getontop.com/payroll-in/colombia) .


Ontop is the Global Workforce Engine, the way companies hire and pay anywhere and the financial home for global workers. Ontop pays more than 4,800 active contractors in Colombia today (Ontop platform data, October 2026), so this guide comes from watching that process run every month, not from theory.


## Key takeaways


- Work performed in Colombia is foreign-source income for US tax purposes, so a US company generally does not withhold US tax or issue a Form 1099 to a Colombian contractor.
- Keep a signed Form W-8BEN (or W-8BEN-E for a company) on file. It goes to you, not to the IRS.
- The United States has no income tax treaty with Colombia, so there is no treaty rate to claim on the form.
- On the Colombian side, the contractor registers with DIAN through the RUT and invoices you with a factura electrónica or a cuenta de cobro, depending on their tax status.
- Services used exclusively abroad can qualify as exempt from Colombian VAT (IVA) under article 481 of the Estatuto Tributario.
- Colombian law presumes an employment contract when someone personally provides a service, so control and subordination, not the contract title, decide classification.
- A contractor of record such as Ontop handles contracts, compliance and USD payouts from $49 per contractor per month.


## What does a US company need to do to pay a contractor in Colombia?


Your side is short. Confirm the person works from Colombia, collect a Form W-8BEN, sign a services agreement, and pay against invoices. Because the work happens outside the United States, the payment is foreign-source income, so there is usually no US withholding and no Form 1099. Keep the paperwork in case of an audit.


### Why there is no 1099


The IRS sources income from personal services by where the work is done. In the words of[IRS Publication 515 (2026)](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p515) , "the place where the services are performed determines the source of the income, regardless of where the contract was made, the place of payment, or the residence of the payer." A developer working from Bogotá earns foreign-source income even when your company is in Delaware and pays from a US bank.


Form 1099-NEC is built for US persons. The[IRS instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i1099mec) point payments to nonresident aliens to Form 1042-S instead, and Form 1042-S only comes into play for US-source income. If your Colombian contractor never works on US soil, neither form applies.


### What the W-8BEN does for you


The W-8BEN is the contractor's certificate of foreign status. According to the[IRS instructions for Form W-8BEN](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iw8ben) , the contractor gives it to you, the payer, and does not send it to the IRS. It generally stays valid until the last day of the third calendar year after it is signed, unless something changes. If the contractor bills through a Colombian company (an S.A.S., for example), ask for a W-8BEN-E instead.


One Colombia-specific detail: Colombia does not appear on the[IRS list of US income tax treaties](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/international-businesses/united-states-income-tax-treaties-a-to-z) . Leave the treaty section of the form blank. It does not change the outcome for work done in Colombia, because that income was never US-source to begin with.


## What does the contractor need to have in place in Colombia?


Your contractor needs a RUT, the tax registration DIAN issues, and a way to invoice you that matches their tax status. Above certain income thresholds they register as responsible for IVA and issue an electronic invoice. Services used exclusively abroad can be IVA-exempt. Income tax is theirs to declare and pay in Colombia.


### RUT and invoicing: factura electrónica or cuenta de cobro


The RUT (Registro Único Tributario) is the identity card of anyone with tax obligations in Colombia. A contractor who invoices foreign clients will almost always need one. Ask for a copy during onboarding. It tells you their legal name, tax ID (NIT) and responsibilities.


How they bill you depends on whether they are responsible for IVA. Under[article 437 of the Estatuto Tributario](https://normograma.dian.gov.co/dian/compilacion/docs/estatuto_tributario.htm) , service providers stay outside the IVA regime only while they meet every condition on the list, including gross income from the activity under 3,500 UVT in the current or previous year. With the UVT set at COP 52,374 for 2026 by[DIAN Resolution 000238 of 2025](https://incp.org.co/publicaciones/infoincp-publicaciones/impuestos/2025/12/dian-fijo-en-52-374-en-valor-de-la-uvt-para-el-ano-gravable-2026/) , that threshold is about COP 183.3 million a year.


Contractors below it often send a cuenta de cobro (a simple payment request). Contractors above it register as IVA responsible and issue a factura electrónica. Do not assume one from the other: DIAN has said that "no es correcto asumir que todos los no responsables de IVA son no obligados a facturar" ([DIAN Oficio 907979 of 2020](https://normograma.dian.gov.co/dian/compilacion/docs/oficio_dian_907979_2020.htm) ). The invoicing duty is a separate question, and it is your contractor's to answer with their accountant.


### IVA on exported services


Article 481(c) of the[Estatuto Tributario](https://normograma.dian.gov.co/dian/compilacion/docs/estatuto_tributario.htm) treats as exempt with right to refund "los servicios que sean prestados en el país y se utilicen exclusivamente en el exterior por empresas o personas sin negocios o actividades en Colombia," as long as the regulatory requirements are met and the exporter keeps documents proving the operation. In practice, a written agreement with your US company is one of the documents your contractor will want. Sign one.


### Income tax and retención en la fuente


Retención en la fuente is Colombia's withholding-at-source system. Article 368 of the Estatuto Tributario names the agents who must withhold: entities and persons who take part in operations where the law expressly requires it. The contractor declares and pays their own income tax to DIAN. Whether a foreign company with no business or presence in Colombia has any withholding duty on these payments depends on the facts of the engagement, so confirm it with a Colombian tax advisor before the first payment.

### What usually breaks with wires


Wires are familiar, which is why most teams start there. The pain shows up later: a payout lands short because an intermediary bank took a cut, the contractor's bank converts at a rate nobody agreed on, and finance spends the first week of every month reconciling. With one contractor, that is annoying. With ten, it is a part-time job.


### Paying in dollars is normal


Most Colombian contractors who work for US companies prefer to be paid in USD and decide when to convert. It protects them from peso swings and keeps the rate decision in their hands. Agree on the currency in the contract, so nobody argues about exchange rates after the fact.


## How do you avoid misclassifying a contractor in Colombia?


Treat classification as a question about how the work actually happens. Colombian labor law presumes an employment contract once someone personally provides a service, so the company has to show the person is genuinely independent. Fixed hours, a boss approving every task and exclusivity point to employment, whatever the contract says.


### The three elements and the presumption


Article 23 of the[Código Sustantivo del Trabajo](https://sidn.ramajudicial.gov.co/SIDN/NORMATIVA/TEXTOS_COMPLETOS/5_DECRETOS/DECRETOS%201950/Decreto%202663%20de%201950%20(C%C3%B3digo%20Sustantivo%20del%20Trabajo).pdf) lists the elements of an employment contract: personal activity, continued subordination and a salary. Article 24 adds the presumption that any personal work relationship is governed by an employment contract. Colombia's Supreme Court treats that presumption as rebuttable: the company can defeat it by showing the person worked autonomously.


The idea behind it is what Colombian lawyers call contrato realidad: reality wins over paperwork. A services agreement that says "independent contractor" will not survive a relationship that looks like a job.


### What genuine independence looks like


- The contractor controls how and when the work gets done, against deliverables or outcomes.
- They use their own equipment and can work for other clients.
- They invoice for services instead of receiving a fixed monthly salary with paid leave.
- They are not slotted into your org chart with a manager, performance reviews and mandatory meetings.


### When you actually need an employee


If the role needs fixed hours, exclusivity and day-to-day direction, you are describing an employee. Hiring one in Colombia requires your own local entity or an employer of record. Ontop does not employ workers on your behalf. It is built for teams that work with contractors, which is how most global teams start. Our page on the[alternative to an EOR for contractor teams](https://www.getontop.com/solutions/eor-alternative-for-contractors) walks through when contractors are the right model and when they are not.


## What is the step-by-step process to pay your first contractor in Colombia?


Five steps cover it: confirm the engagement is a real contract, collect the W-8BEN and RUT, sign the services agreement, agree on how invoices arrive, and set up the payout. Done once, the monthly run takes minutes. Most delays come from skipping the agreement or the currency decision at the start.


1. **Scope the work as a service.** Define deliverables, rate (hourly, monthly retainer or per project) and currency. Avoid fixed schedules and exclusivity.
2. **Collect documents.** A signed W-8BEN (or W-8BEN-E), a copy of the contractor's RUT, and a national ID or passport for your records.
3. **Sign a services agreement.** Cover scope, IP assignment, confidentiality, termination and payment terms. It also supports the contractor's IVA export treatment.
4. **Agree on invoicing.** Factura electrónica or cuenta de cobro, monthly or by milestone, with a clear due date.
5. **Choose the payout rail and schedule it.** Know the all-in cost of each payment, including FX, before the first one goes out.

## Frequently asked questions


### Do I need to send a 1099 to a contractor in Colombia?


No, as long as the contractor is not a US person and does all the work from outside the United States. That income is foreign-source, so Form 1099-NEC does not apply. Keep a signed Form W-8BEN on file instead.


### Do I have to withhold US tax when I pay a Colombian contractor?


Generally no. US withholding on payments to foreign persons applies to US-source income, and IRS Publication 515 sources service income by where the work is performed. If any work happens while the contractor is physically in the United States, talk to a tax advisor about that portion.


### Can I pay a contractor in Colombia in US dollars?


Yes. Many Colombian contractors prefer USD and convert to pesos when it suits them. Set the currency in the contract. With Ontop, payouts land in USD in the contractor's Global Account.


### Does my Colombian contractor charge me IVA?


Usually not for work you use outside Colombia. Article 481(c) of the Estatuto Tributario treats services used exclusively abroad by companies without business in Colombia as exempt, provided the regulatory requirements are met. Your contractor and their accountant handle that treatment.


### What if I want to hire my contractor as a full-time employee in Colombia?


Then you need a local entity or an employer of record, because only an employer can run Colombian payroll and benefits. Ontop does not employ people. It works for contractor relationships, which is how most global teams start.
